abstract: Multi-tissue transcriptome resources are central to understanding tissue-specific regulation and inter-individual variation. Realistically, most tissues are measured in only a subset of donors, especially for less accessible tissues such as brain and heart. Accurately imputing gene expression values for such tissues, while accounting for individual heterogeneity, remains a daunting challenge. Here, we present BRIDGE (Body-wide Representation via Inter-tissue Decoding of Gene Expression), a lightweight framework that imputes donor-specific and tissue-specific expression measures using contrastive learning. When tested on real-world expression data from the Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) consortium, BRIDGE recovered donor-specific variation more accurately than existing state-of-the-art methods while improving overall accuracy, with the largest advantage found in the most inaccessible tissues. We provide the BRIDGE-imputed completed GTEx v11 donor x tissue xgene expression tensor as a resource to the broader research community.
